sentences.text:
Akhilesh Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 22 February,
2022

Bench: Anjuli Palo
The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Crr No. 123 of 2022 (Akhilesh Jain And Others Vs The
State Of Madhya Pradesh) Jabalpur, Dated : 22-02-2022 Shri Pradeep Naveriya, counsel for
the applicants.
Shri Om Prakash Patel, Pl for the State.
The revision seems to be arguable, therefore, admitted for hearing.

Heard on I.A. No. 746/2022,
which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicants.
The applicants have been convicted by the appellate Court under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for six months with fine of Rs. 1000/- each with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the sentence awarded to the applicants is six months.

The applicants are in custody and disposal of this revision will take considerable time,
therefore, the custodial sentence of the applicants may be suspended and they may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for bail.
Considering the period of sentence awarded to the applicants and other facts and circumstances of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) each with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence imposed upon the applicants shall remain suspended and they shall be released on bail for securing their presence before the trial Court concerned on 11.7.2022 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of this revision.
List for final hearing in due course.
(SMT. ANJULI PALO) JUDGE PB Akhilesh Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 22 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6801015/
